vectors.name: exclude_overlapping_squares
vectors._derivation: XOR of [0,10]^2 and [5,15]^2 is the two L-shapes left after removing the [5,10]^2 overlap: each of area 100-25 = 75, total 150. They meet only at the isolated points (10,5) and (5,10), so the derived-correct representation is TWO simple rings, which is what ring_count pins. Both ports now emit exactly that: (10,5) (15,5) (15,15) (5,15) (5,10) (10,10) with shoelace -25+150+150-25-50-50 = 150 hence area 75, and (0,0) (10,0) (10,5) (5,5) (5,10) (0,10) with shoelace 0+50+25+25+50+0 = 150 hence area 75. The GAP THAT USED TO LIVE HERE (both ports emitting ONE self-touching twelve-vertex ring, because connect_edges cannot tell which of two regions touching at a pinch vertex it is on) is CLOSED by the split-at-repeated-vertex post-pass in boolean.rs split_pinched_rings / Boolean.swift splitPinchedRings, which was unblocked by the carried-rule ruling: it needed Swift's Path to carry a fill rule first, so that a multi-ring result could be materialised the same way in both ports. See transcripts/BOOLEAN.md.

vectors.name: subtract_from_evenodd_declared_donut
vectors._derivation: THE CARRIED-RULE HONESTY PAIR, half one. Operand A is two nested CCW rings, [0,20]^2 and [5,15]^2, DECLARED even-odd — so it is a donut of area 400 - 100 = 300 and the middle is NOT part of it. B is the bottom strip [0,20]x[0,3] of area 60, which lies wholly inside the outer ring and wholly BELOW the hole (the hole starts at y=5), so it never touches it. A - B is therefore the rectangle [0,20]x[3,20] (area 20*17 = 340) minus the still-detached hole [5,15]^2 (area 100) = 240, as two rings. The sample at (10,10) sits in the hole and must be OUTSIDE. Paired with subtract_from_nonzero_declared_solid: identical geometry, opposite declared rule, different answer — which is the whole point of carrying the rule instead of fixing it.

vectors.name: subtract_from_nonzero_declared_solid
vectors._derivation: THE CARRIED-RULE HONESTY PAIR, half two, and the correctness argument that decided the ruling. The SAME operand A rings, DECLARED nonzero — the SVG default, so this is what an imported fill-rule=nonzero path means. Inside the inner ring the winding is +1+1 = 2, so A is a SOLID square of area 400 with no hole at all. Subtracting the same strip leaves the rectangle [0,20]x[3,20]: area 20*17 = 340, ONE ring. The sample at (10,10) is now INSIDE. Before the carried-rule ruling the algorithm layer fixed even-odd, so this document's declared rule was silently discarded and the boolean op cut a hole the artist never asked for; this vector is the gate that keeps that from coming back.
